newsitem.title: USA: Technician cites defensive signals in Nasdaq index.
newsitem.headline: Technician cites defensive signals in Nasdaq index.

text.p: The Nasdaq Composite index may be near record high levels, but one technician says there are signs in the market that point to taking a defensive position.

Michael McCarthy, president of McCarthy Market Research in New York, told investment advisers at a conference here that a dwindling number of stocks in the index making new highs points to eroding strength in the market.

"Even though the market is near record levels, the number of stocks within the index making new highs is declining," McCarthy said in an interview after he appeared as a panelist at the Society of Asset Allocators and Fund Timers conference.

Nasdaq peaked on June 5 at 1,249.15 on a closing basis, but the number of stocks making new highs peaked May 14, with 499 making new highs that day, McCarthy said. By June 5, the number of new highs had dropped to 303, he said.
From May 14 to June 5, the Nasdaq rose 1.2 percent, but during that same time, the number of stocks making new highs had decreased 39 percent, he said.
From its June peak to the bottom July 24 at 1,042.37 on a closing basis, the market declined 16.6 percent.
Even though the market made a new closing high again in October at 1,256.36, the number of new highs at that point was only 174, down 65 percent from the May 14 peak in new highs, McCarthy said.
"What it means is that a handful of stocks in the index are leading the market," he said.
Since the market does not have a lot of support, it will be susceptible to sharp declines that seem to come out of nowhere, he said.

"But it does not appear to be the makings of a crash," McCarthy added, because most short-term interest rates are lower now than they were a year ago. Major market declines tend to occur in an environment when interest rates are rising and investors have a safer alternative to the stock market, McCarthy said. -Chris Romans (312) 408-8750
